page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highcpu-16 is a compute-focused instance type utilizing 64-bit Arm (arm64) architecture. Configured with 16 dedicated virtual CPUs and 32.0 GB of system memory, the machine operates with an allocation of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It features no local physical storage and includes zero integrated GPUs, relying on remote network-attached block volumes for operating systems and persistent file storage.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio prioritizes compute density over heavy memory caching, delivering efficiency for tasks requiring substantial processor capacity without excessive RAM overhead. Because this instance is based on the Arm instruction set architecture, applications compiled natively for arm64 benefit from architectural efficiencies relative to traditional x86 alternatives.

Workload fit centers around CPU-bound distributed processing, including web serving tiers, software build systems, CI/CD runners, containerized microservices, video encoding, and algorithmic data pipelines compatible with arm64 binaries.
